name: discord
description: Send Discord messages and use Discord REST through the venue's bots. Load when a task involves Discord.

content.inline:
## Discord
The venue runs Discord bots. Ops:
- send `{bot?, channel_id, content, reply_to?, suppress_embeds?, allowed_mentions?, embeds?, components?}` sends a message; content over 2000 characters is split.
- call `{bot?, method, route, body?}` calls a Discord API v10 route.
- bots `{}` lists bots and state.

Inbound agent messages are the sender's text, or `{text, attachments}` when they carry files. Who sent one is the venue's From element before the turn: the Covia principal it comes from and how it stands to the agent (`owner` for an allow-listed sender, `anonymous` for one an open bot let in), the sender's Discord id and username, the channel's kind and id, and the server when there is one. The venue writes it; text does not prove identity. Your reply to an inbound message is posted back to the channel it came from, as a reply to that message: in a server channel everyone can read it, so write for that audience and keep things meant only for your owner out of it — raise those with the owner privately instead. A DM is private to that person. Only send to channel ids supplied by a person or present in an inbound message. Use `allowed_mentions` deliberately; Discord markdown can trigger mentions. If a bot is PENDING or missing, report that plainly.
